decode: Jose Rizal trained in ophthalmology in Paris under LOUIS DE WECKER (1885).
ow: R.M. Clark set up the Manila clinic; he did not train Rizal.
Otto Becker trained Rizal in Germany, not Paris.
Correct. Louis de Wecker in Paris.
Ernst Fuchs trained Rizal in Vienna, not Paris.

q: The first optometric clinic doing refraction and the first lens-grinding shop in Manila were established in 1902 by:
w: R.M. Clark set up the first refracting clinic and lens-grinding shop in Manila in 1902, fifteen years before the profession was regulated.
k: R.M. Clark, 1902: first refracting clinic.
decode: The first refracting clinic and lens-grinding shop in Manila (1902) were established by R.M. CLARK.
ow: Justo Gonzalez is not credited with the 1902 clinic.
Federico Sarabia Sr. is cited as the reputed first Filipino optometrist, not the 1902 clinic founder.
Correct. R.M. Clark, 1902.
William G. Moore is not credited with the 1902 clinic.

q: The first university-affiliated optometry college in the Philippines was:
w: CEU opened the first university-affiliated optometry college in 1928, with Dr. Roy A. Thorson as first dean. The Philippine College of Optometry was the first school overall.
k: CEU 1928 = first university-affiliated college.
decode: The first university-affiliated optometry college was CENTRO ESCOLAR UNIVERSITY (1928).
ow: De Ocampo Memorial College is not the first university-affiliated one.
The Manila College of Optometry is not the first university-affiliated one.
Correct. CEU (1928).
The Philippine College of Optometry was the first school overall, not university-affiliated.

q: Registration Certificate No. 1 was issued in 1918 to:
w: PRC records show Certificate No. 1 issued 11 March 1918 to Dr. Manuel Sabater. Federico Sarabia Sr. is often cited as the reputed first, being the first Filipino to study optometry in the US.
k: Certificate No. 1 = Manuel Sabater (1918).
decode: Registration Certificate No. 1 (1918) was issued to Dr. MANUEL SABATER.
ow: Correct. Manuel Sabater (1918).
Bibiana Roxas de Jesus did not hold Certificate No. 1.
Justo Gonzalez did not hold Certificate No. 1.
Federico Sarabia Sr. is the reputed first, but Certificate No. 1 went to Sabater.

q: The 1979 merger of OAP, PODA and PROA produced:
w: The PRC wanted a single association, so OAP, PODA and PROA merged into SOP in 1979, with about 37 OAP chapters joining.
k: 1979: OAP + PODA + PROA = SOP.
decode: The 1979 merger of OAP, PODA, and PROA produced the SOP.
ow: APCO is a later regional body, not the 1979 merger result.
The WCO is the world council, not the 1979 merger.
IFAPAO is the Asian-Pacific federation, not the 1979 merger.
Correct. OAP + PODA + PROA = SOP (1979).

q: IFAPAO was founded at the 1st Asian-Pacific Optometric Congress held in 1978 in:
w: The 1st APOC in Manila, July 1978, founded IFAPAO, which later became APCO. Its first president, elected at the 2nd APOC in Bali, was Claro M. Cinco.
k: IFAPAO founded 1978, 1st APOC Manila.
decode: IFAPAO was founded at the 1st Asian-Pacific Optometric Congress in 1978 in MANILA.
ow: Toronto did not host the 1st APOC.
Bali hosted the 2nd APOC, not the founding.
Sydney did not host the 1st APOC.
Correct. Manila, 1978.

q: The first International Optometrist of the Year, in 1988, was:
w: Dr. Claro M. Cinco received the first award in 1988. Later recipients include Svein Hommerstad and Henry W. Hofstetter, of the Hofstetter amplitude formulas.
k: First International Optometrist of the Year: Claro M. Cinco (1988).
decode: The first International Optometrist of the Year (1988) was Dr. CLARO M. CINCO.
ow: Svein Hommerstad was a later recipient.
Henry W. Hofstetter was a later recipient.
Correct. Claro M. Cinco (1988).
Justo Gonzalez did not receive the first award.

q: Under the Code of Ethics, using the title 'Doctor' is unethical unless it is:
w: The Code requires 'Dr.' to be qualified so the public is not misled into thinking the practitioner is a physician.
k: 'Dr.' must be qualified with optometry/optometrist.
decode: Using the title 'Doctor' is unethical unless QUALIFIED with 'optometrist' (so the public is not misled).
ow: Board approval is not the requirement.
Correct. 'Dr.' must be qualified with optometry/optometrist.
The license number is not the qualifier.
It is not merely limited to clinic use.

q: Displaying a name or title at street level is unethical when the letters exceed:
w: Letters larger than six inches at street level are treated as advertising that degrades the professional image, as are signboards with pictures of eyes or eyeglasses.
k: Street-level lettering limit = six inches.
decode: Street-level lettering is unethical when the letters exceed SIX inches.
ow: Correct. The limit is six inches.
The limit is six inches, not two.
The limit is six inches, not four.
The limit is six inches, not twelve.

q: A consultant who receives a referred patient must:
o: Return the patient to the referrer
Report the referrer to the Board
w: The Code requires the consultant to return the patient. Treating a colleague's patient in an emergency is allowed, but the patient is returned afterward.
k: Consultant returns the patient to the referrer.
decode: A consultant who receives a referred patient must RETURN the patient to the referrer.
ow: Correct. Return the patient to the referrer.
The consultant does not bill the referring optometrist.
The consultant does not report the referrer to the Board.
The consultant does not take over the patient's care.

q: Under the Code, a patient's character flaws learned during care are:
o: Held in trust, disclosed only by law
w: The AOA supplement holds such knowledge in trust. Confidentiality yields only to a legal requirement.
k: Patient's character flaws held in trust.
decode: A patient's character flaws learned during care are HELD IN TRUST, disclosed only when the law requires.
ow: They are not shared with the next practitioner freely.
They are not reportable to the association.
They are not recorded in the public register.
Correct. Held in trust, disclosed only by law.

q: Which act is expressly unethical under the Code?
o: Charging by skill and time spent
w: The list of unethical acts includes lay examiners, soliciting patients, house-to-house canvassing, mobile canvassing units, advertising fees, and practicing under a name other than the one on the certificate.
k: Lay persons must never do the visual examination.
decode: Letting a LAY PERSON examine is expressly unethical under the Code.
ow: Correct. A lay person must never do the visual examination.
Referring a difficult case onward is proper.
Charging by skill and time spent is proper.
Joining a professional association is proper.

q: Under the Code, an optometrist discovering a corrupt or dishonest colleague should:
w: The duty toward other optometrists includes exposing corrupt or dishonest members to the Board, alongside cooperation and avoiding derogatory hints about colleagues.
k: Duty to expose dishonest colleagues to the Board.
decode: On discovering a corrupt or dishonest colleague, the optometrist should EXPOSE them to the Board.
ow: Saying nothing out of collegiality is not the duty.
Advertising the fact publicly is improper.
Correct. Expose them to the Board.
Confronting privately only is insufficient.

q: May an optometrist refuse to accept a patient, even as the only practitioner in town?
w: The privilege to practice does not compel him to accept anyone; nothing in the Code forces service even in an emergency. Once he accepts a case needing continuing care, though, he must see it through.
k: Right to choose patients is inherent in the privilege.
decode: An optometrist MAY refuse to accept a patient (he chooses his patients), even as the only practitioner in town.
ow: Prior Board approval is not required to decline.
Refusal is not always unethical.
Nothing in the Code compels service even in an emergency.
Correct. He may choose his patients.

q: An optometrist's instruments and library are:
o: Exempt from execution as tools of the trade
w: Exemption of instruments and library from execution is a right incidental to the privilege to practice, protecting the tools of the trade from creditors.
k: Instruments and library exempt from execution.
decode: An optometrist's instruments and library are EXEMPT FROM EXECUTION as tools of the trade.
ow: They are not owned by the PRC.
They are not transferable only to optometrists.
Correct. Exempt from execution as tools of the trade.
They are not taxable as inventory in this context.

q: The classic statement of a patient's right to self-determination comes from:
w: Justice Cardozo wrote in Schloendorff (1914) that every adult of sound mind has the right to determine what shall be done with his own body. Natanson v. Kline and Salgo v. Leland Stanford developed it further.
k: Schloendorff (Cardozo, 1914) = right to self-determination.
decode: The classic statement of the patient's right to self-determination comes from SCHLOENDORFF (Cardozo, 1914).
ow: People v. Pomar concerns police power, not self-determination.
Correct. Schloendorff (Cardozo, 1914).
Safian v. Aetna concerns breach of contract, not self-determination.
Picart v. Smith is the negligence foreseeability test.

q: The optometrist-patient relationship is described as fiduciary, meaning it is built on:
w: A fiduciary relationship obliges the optometrist to disclose the true facts; misrepresentation makes him liable. The relationship is also contractual, so a procedure outside that contract is void.
k: Fiduciary = built on trust, duty to disclose.
decode: The optometrist-patient relationship is FIDUCIARY, built on TRUST and full disclosure.
ow: Professional courtesy is not the fiduciary basis.
A written fee agreement is not the fiduciary basis.
Correct. Built on trust and full disclosure.
It rests on more than statutory duty alone.

q: Consent is NOT required when the law itself compels a procedure, such as:
w: Compulsory immunization under RA 3573 and PD 996 is compelled by law under the state's police power, and refusal is punishable. The other exception is a genuine emergency.
k: Compulsory immunization (RA 3573, PD 996) needs no consent.
decode: Consent is not required when the law compels a procedure, such as COMPULSORY IMMUNIZATION (RA 3573, PD 996).
ow: Correct. Compulsory immunization needs no consent.
A cycloplegic refraction requires consent.
A contact lens fitting requires consent.
A vision screening requires consent.

q: A competent patient who refuses sight-saving care:
o: May be reported to the Board
May refuse; he is master of his own body
Loses the right to any care
w: The right to refuse holds even when treatment could save life or sight. The state can still compel narrow public-health measures such as immunization under police power.
k: Competent patient may refuse even sight-saving care.
decode: A competent patient who refuses sight-saving care MAY REFUSE; he is master of his own body.
ow: Refusing care is not itself a reportable matter.
Correct. He may refuse; he is master of his own body.
He does not lose the right to any care.
He must not be treated against his refusal.

q: When an optometrist withdraws from a case, he must:
w: The relationship ends on recovery, patient withdrawal or optometrist withdrawal. On withdrawing he passes records to the successor and informs the patient. The patient may discharge him at any time.
k: On withdrawal: hand over records, inform the patient.
decode: When an optometrist withdraws from a case, he must HAND OVER records and INFORM the patient.
ow: He is not obliged to continue care for a fixed 30 days.
Board clearance is not required to withdraw.
He need not refund all fees already paid.
Correct. Hand over records and inform the patient.

q: The PRC is composed of one Chairperson and how many Commissioners?
w: One full-time Chairperson and two full-time Commissioners, appointed by the President for a seven-year term with no reappointment.
k: PRC = 1 Chair + 2 Commissioners.
decode: The PRC is composed of one Chairperson and TWO Commissioners.
ow: Correct. One Chair and two Commissioners.
There are two Commissioners, not four.
There are two Commissioners, not one.
There are two Commissioners, not three.

q: The term of a PRC Chairperson or Commissioner is:
w: The PRC term is seven years with no reappointment. Do not swap this with the Board of Optometry's five-year non-renewable term: it is a classic trap.
k: PRC term 7 years; Board term 5 years.
decode: A PRC Chairperson or Commissioner serves a 7-year term with NO reappointment.
ow: Correct. 7 years, no reappointment.
It is 7 years no reappointment, not 6 renewable once.
5 years non-renewable is the Board of Optometry term, not the PRC.
It is 7 years, not 3 renewable.

q: The minimum age for a PRC Chairperson or Commissioner is:
w: A PRC Chairperson or Commissioner must be at least 40, hold a valid license, and have at least five years of executive or management experience. The Board of Optometry minimum is 35.
k: PRC official: 40 years old, 5 years management experience.
decode: The minimum age for a PRC Chairperson or Commissioner is 40 (the Board of Optometry minimum is 35).
ow: 30 is below the PRC minimum.
35 is the Board of Optometry minimum, not the PRC.
Correct. At least 40 years old.
45 exceeds the minimum.

q: The PRC was created by which decree?
w: PD 223, as amended by PD 657, created the PRC and moved supervision of the boards from the Bureau of Civil Service. RA 8981, the PRC Modernization Act of 2000, later reorganized it and repealed PD 223.
k: PRC created by PD 223; modernized by RA 8981 (2000).
decode: The PRC was created by PD 223 (modernized by RA 8981, 2000).
ow: PD 996 concerns compulsory immunization, not the PRC.
RA 7722 is the Higher Education Act.
RA 3573 concerns reporting of communicable diseases.
Correct. PD 223 created the PRC.

q: The 'Board of Examiners in Optometry' was renamed the 'Board of Optometry' by:
w: PD 223 as amended by PD 657 renamed the body. RA 8050 governs the Board's present composition and functions but did not rename it.
k: PD 223/657 renamed it the Board of Optometry.
decode: PD 223 (as amended by PD 657) renamed the body the BOARD OF OPTOMETRY.
ow: RA 8050 governs the Board's present functions but did not rename it.
Correct. PD 223/657 renamed it.
RA 8981 modernized the PRC but did not rename the Board.
RA 1998 is the old optometry law, not the renaming decree.

q: An administrative decision of the Board, once appealed to the PRC, may be elevated to the:
w: Administrative cases run Board → PRC (within 15 days) → Office of the President. Criminal and civil cases go through the courts and appeal to the Court of Appeals.
k: Administrative: Board → PRC → Office of the President.
decode: An administrative decision, once appealed to the PRC, may be elevated to the OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT.
ow: Correct. Board then PRC then Office of the President.
The Supreme Court is not the next administrative step.
The Court of Appeals handles criminal/civil, not this administrative chain.
The Regional Trial Court is not the administrative appeal path.

q: Under PMA v. Dr. Cruz, the President is:
o: Bound to appoint the top nominee
Not bound by the association's nominees
w: The Court held a recommendation is only advice, so the President is not bound by the list the integrated organization submits.
k: PMA v. Cruz: nominations only advise the President.
decode: Under PMA v. Dr. Cruz, the President is NOT BOUND by the association's nominees (a recommendation is only advice).
ow: He is not barred from rejecting nominees.
He is not bound to appoint the top nominee.
He is not required to consult the DOH.
Correct. The President is not bound by the nominees.

q: Under PRC Resolution No. 114, a criminal action against a non-professional practising illegally is filed with the:
w: The Board has primary responsibility for starting the action, which is filed with the Provincial or City Fiscal, who files the information in court on a prima facie case.
k: Illegal practice: file with the Provincial/City Fiscal.
decode: Under PRC Resolution No. 114, a criminal action against an illegal (non-professional) practitioner is filed with the PROVINCIAL or CITY FISCAL.
ow: Correct. File with the Provincial or City Fiscal.
The PRC Legal Division does not file the criminal information.
The Court of Appeals is an appellate court, not where it is filed.
The Board starts the action but files it with the Fiscal.

q: The practice of optometry is a privilege the state grants under its:
w: Police power is the legislature's power to pass reasonable laws for public welfare, health, morality and safety. People v. Pomar and US v. Gomez Jesus are the classic cases.
k: Practice is a privilege under police power.
decode: The practice of optometry is a privilege the state grants under its POLICE POWER.
ow: Eminent domain concerns taking property, not licensing.
Correct. Under police power.
Parens patriae concerns the state as guardian, not licensing generally.
The power of taxation is not the licensing basis.

q: Why can a corporation not practice optometry?
o: It is barred by the Corporation Code
It cannot afford the license fees
It cannot meet the personal qualifications
w: A corporation cannot hold good moral character, a degree or an oath, so it cannot practice directly, and it may not do indirectly what it cannot do directly by hiring optometrists to sell lenses.
k: Corporation cannot practice: no personal qualifications.
decode: A corporation cannot practice optometry because it cannot meet the PERSONAL qualifications (good moral character, a degree, an oath).
ow: The bar is the lack of personal qualifications, not merely a Corporation Code prohibition.
Owning instruments is not the reason.
License-fee affordability is not the reason.
Correct. It cannot meet the personal qualifications.

q: An optometrist employed by a non-optometrist may lawfully serve:
o: Anyone, if a license is shown
The general public in the store
w: An in-house or retainer optometrist may serve the employer's own employees, not the general public. An optometrist who aids or abets a lay corporation's practice risks suspension or revocation.
k: In-house optometrist serves employees, not the public.
decode: An optometrist employed by a non-optometrist may lawfully serve the EMPLOYER'S OWN EMPLOYEES, not the general public.
ow: Not walk-in patients generally.
Not anyone merely because a license is shown.
Correct. The employer's own employees.
Not the general public in the store.

q: A faith healer who prays over a patient's eyes, then picks up diagnostic instruments, is:
w: The Constitution protects the freedom to believe absolutely and the freedom to act conditionally. Prayer alone is religion; using diagnostic instruments or optical devices crosses into illegal practice.
k: Prayer is religion; instruments make it illegal practice.
decode: A faith healer who prays and then picks up DIAGNOSTIC INSTRUMENTS is engaged in ILLEGAL PRACTICE (prayer is religion; instruments cross into practice).
ow: Correct. Using instruments makes it illegal practice.
It is more than an ethical breach; it is illegal practice.
Section 5 does not exempt a faith healer using instruments.
Religious freedom protects belief, not unlicensed practice with instruments.

q: The test for negligence, from Picart v. Smith, asks whether:
o: A specialist would have done better
A prudent person would have foreseen the harm
w: Picart v. Smith sets the reasonable-person standard: if a prudent person in the actor's place would foresee harm, the law imposes a duty to take precaution, and failing to do so is negligence.
k: Picart v. Smith: the prudent-person foreseeability test.
decode: The test for negligence (Picart v. Smith) asks whether a PRUDENT PERSON would have foreseen the harm.
ow: It is the prudent-person standard, not a specialist-comparison test.
Correct. Whether a prudent person would foresee the harm.
Patient consent is a separate issue, not the negligence test.
An unfavorable result alone is not negligence.

q: An optometrist is liable for breach of contract only if he:
o: Specifically promised a cure or result
w: Safian v. Aetna: failing to cure is not a breach when no cure was ever contracted. In a breach-of-contract suit expert testimony is not required and pain and suffering is not an element. Never guarantee results.
k: Breach of contract needs a promised result.
decode: An optometrist is liable for breach of contract only if he SPECIFICALLY PROMISED a cure or result.
ow: An excessive fee is a fee dispute, not a breach of a promised result.
Failing to refer promptly may be negligence, not breach of a promised result.
Correct. Breach of contract needs a promised result.
Failing to cure is not a breach when no cure was contracted.

q: Damage caused by fault or negligence where no prior contract exists is a:
w: Article 2176 of the Civil Code: whoever by act or omission causes damage through fault or negligence must pay, and absent a prior contract that fault is a quasi-delict, or tort.
k: No contract + negligence = quasi-delict (Art. 2176).
decode: Damage from fault or negligence with NO prior contract is a QUASI-DELICT (Civil Code Art. 2176).
ow: Correct. No contract plus negligence is a quasi-delict.
It is a civil wrong, not merely an administrative offence.
Breach of contract requires a prior contract.
It is a quasi-delict, not necessarily a criminal felony.

q: Written defamation is libel; spoken defamation is:
w: Article 353 of the Revised Penal Code defines defamation as a public and malicious imputation causing dishonor. Libel is written (Art. 355), slander is oral, and the elements include malice and bad faith.
k: Libel written; slander oral.
decode: Written defamation is libel; SPOKEN defamation is SLANDER.
ow: Correct. Spoken defamation is slander.
Fraud is deceit for gain, not spoken defamation.
Perjury is lying under oath, not defamation.
Deceit is misrepresentation, not spoken defamation.

q: If a patient dies owing fees, the claim runs first against the:
w: Article 291 of the Civil Code orders the claim: spouse, then descendant of nearest degree, then ascendant of nearest degree, then brothers and sisters. Medical care counts as 'support' under Article 290.
k: Fee claim order: spouse → descendant → ascendant → siblings.
decode: If a patient dies owing fees, the claim runs first against the SPOUSE (Civil Code Art. 291 order: spouse, descendant, ascendant, siblings).
ow: The nearest descendant comes after the spouse.
Correct. The spouse is first in the order.
The nearest ascendant comes after descendants.
Brothers and sisters come last.

q: A patient may lawfully refuse to pay when:
o: He has no money at present
A third party promised to pay
A contingent fee did not succeed
w: Valid grounds are: the service was expressly free, the fee was contingent on a success that did not come despite the patient's cooperation, or the treatment differed from what was agreed. A third party's promise never releases the patient.
k: Contingent fee + failure = patient may refuse to pay.
decode: A patient may lawfully refuse to pay when a CONTINGENT FEE did not succeed (despite the patient's cooperation).
ow: Having no money at present is not a lawful ground to refuse.
A third party's promise never releases the patient.
A disappointing result alone is not a ground to refuse.
Correct. A failed contingent fee is a valid ground.

q: On a referral, the fee of the consultant is owed by:
w: The attending optometrist is not liable for the consultant's fee. The patient, being of legal age and sound mind, is primarily liable.
k: Consultant's fee is owed by the patient, not the referrer.
decode: On a referral, the consultant's fee is owed by the PATIENT (not the referring optometrist).
ow: The integrated organization does not owe the fee.
The PRC does not owe the fee.
The referring optometrist is not liable for the consultant's fee.
Correct. The patient owes the consultant's fee.

q: Section 29's continuing-education condition for license renewal was repealed by:
w: Section 20 of RA 8981, the PRC Modernization Act of 2000, repealed the CPD-for-renewal rule as RA 8050 first wrote it, so CPD is not a hard statutory condition of base renewal. The three-year cycle itself remains.
k: RA 8981 repealed Sec 29's CPD-for-renewal rule.
decode: Section 29's continuing-education-for-renewal condition was repealed by RA 8981 (PRC Modernization Act, 2000).
ow: PD 223 created the PRC; it did not repeal Sec 29.
RA 8050 wrote the rule; it did not repeal it.
RA 7722 is the Higher Education Act.
Correct. RA 8981 repealed Sec 29's CPD-for-renewal rule.

q: A candidate scores a 78% general average but gets 48% in one subject. Under RA 8050, the candidate:
w: Section 20 requires at least a 75% average AND no rating below 50% in any subject. The 48% disqualifies despite the high average.
k: Section 20 requires at least a 75% average AND no rating below 50% in any subject.
decode: A 78% average with a 48% in one subject FAILS: Sec 20 requires at least 75% AND no rating below 50%.
ow: The 48% disqualifies despite the high average.
There is no conditional pass; the 48% fails.
Correct. Fails on the sub-50% subject.
There is no single-subject retake; the candidate fails.

q: The Board of Optometry is composed of how many members, and from how many nominees?
w: , appointed by the President on PRC recommendation, from the accredited national organization's list.
k: , appointed by the President on PRC recommendation, from the accredited national organization's list.
decode: The Board of Optometry is 5 members from 10 nominees (appointed by the President on PRC recommendation).
ow: It is 5 from 10, not 3 from 6.
It is 5 from 10, not 7 from 14.
It is 5 from 10, not 5 from 5.
Correct. 5 members from 10 nominees.

q: An optometrist places an ad claiming "lower fees than any clinic in town." Under RA 8050 this is:
o: Allowed if the claim is true
w: Section 32(c) prohibits advertising conveying that one optometrist is better or charges lower fees. Truth is no defense.
k: Section 32(c) prohibits advertising conveying that one optometrist is better or charges lower fees.
decode: An ad claiming 'lower fees than any clinic' is a PROHIBITED ACT (Sec 32c); truth is no defense.
ow: It is not allowed only in print media.
Board approval does not permit it.
Correct. A prohibited act.
Truth does not make it allowed.

q: A person convicted of unauthorized practice of optometry faces what penalty?
o: A fine only, up to P5,000
w: Section 33 sets imprisonment of 1 to 8 years, or a fine of P10,000 to P40,000, or both, at the court's discretion, plus applicable administrative penalties.
k: Section 33 sets imprisonment of 1 to 8 years, or a fine of P10,000 to P40,000, or both, at the court's…
decode: Unauthorized practice is punished under Sec 33: 1 to 8 years, or P10,000 to P40,000, or both.
ow: A community service order is not the statutory penalty.
It is more than license suspension alone.
Correct. 1 to 8 years or P10,000 to P40,000 (or both).
It is more than a P5,000 fine.

q: An optometrist instills a dilating drop without telling the patient it will blur near vision and cause light sensitivity, and without asking permission. Which principle is violated?
w: Failing to disclose effects and obtain consent violates the patient's right to make an informed decision.
k: Failing to disclose effects and obtain consent violates the patient's right to make an informed decision.
decode: Instilling a dilating drop without disclosing effects or asking permission violates AUTONOMY.
ow: Collegiality concerns colleagues, not patient consent.
Correct. It violates the patient's autonomy.
Justice is fairness, not the consent issue.
Beneficence is doing good, not the consent issue.

q: Choosing not to fit extended-wear lenses in a non-compliant patient with a history of microbial keratitis primarily reflects which principle?
w: Avoiding a foreseeable harm whose risk outweighs the benefit is "do no harm."
k: Avoiding a foreseeable harm whose risk outweighs the benefit is "do no harm."
decode: Declining extended-wear lenses in a non-compliant patient with prior microbial keratitis reflects NON-MALEFICENCE.
ow: Autonomy is the patient's right to decide, not the clinician's avoid-harm duty.
Correct. Avoiding foreseeable harm is non-maleficence.
Justice is fairness, not the avoid-harm issue.
Confidentiality concerns privacy, not this decision.

q: A competent adult refuses referral for a suspicious optic disc. The most ethical action is:
o: Refuse to see the patient again
Report the patient to the Board
Override the refusal and refer anyway
w: Autonomy allows refusal, but beneficence and non-maleficence require continued care: document, re-counsel, and keep monitoring.
k: Autonomy allows refusal, but beneficence and non-maleficence require continued care: document, re-counsel…
decode: When a competent adult refuses referral for a suspicious disc, the ethical action is DOCUMENT, RE-COUNSEL, and keep MONITORING.
ow: Refusing to see the patient again is abandonment.
Reporting the patient to the Board is inappropriate.
Overriding the refusal violates autonomy.
Correct. Document, re-counsel, keep monitoring.

q: Providing a faster, lesser examination to a PhilHealth patient than to a private patient with the same complaint violates:
w: Distributive justice requires the same standard of care regardless of ability to pay or status.
k: Distributive justice requires the same standard of care regardless of ability to pay or status.
decode: Giving a PhilHealth patient a lesser examination than a private patient violates JUSTICE (equal standard of care).
ow: Beneficence is doing good, not the equal-standard issue.
Non-maleficence is avoiding harm, not the equal-standard issue.
Correct. It violates distributive justice.
Autonomy is the patient's right to decide, not equal standard.

q: Under RA 8050 Section 40, which duty corresponds most directly to the principle of non-maleficence?
o: Consider the visual welfare of the public as the primary responsibility
Refer for medical attention when indicated
Render services with equal diligence to all
w: Referring when a condition exceeds your competence prevents harm, the core of non-maleficence. Visual welfare is beneficence; equal diligence is justice; confidentiality protects trust/autonomy.
k: Referring when a condition exceeds your competence prevents harm, the core of non-maleficence.
decode: The Sec 40 duty 'refer for medical attention when indicated' maps to NON-MALEFICENCE (referring beyond competence prevents harm).
ow: Visual welfare of the public is beneficence.
Correct. Referring when indicated is non-maleficence.
Confidentiality protects trust/privacy, not referral.
Equal diligence to all is justice.

q: What is the correct order of registrations to open a sole-proprietorship optometry clinic?

w: Care beyond one's scope warrants appropriate referral. Ignoring, over-treating or concealing endangers the patient and breaches ethics.
k: Scope-of-practice questions almost always answer "refer appropriately."
decode: If a condition requires another professional's services, the optometrist should REFER the patient appropriately.
ow: Hiding the finding is unethical.
Correct. Refer the patient appropriately.
Continuing treatment indefinitely beyond scope endangers the patient.
Ignoring it is unethical.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: Once an optometrist has formally undertaken a case, the optometrist should:
o: Abandon the patient immediately without notice or onward referral
Continue appropriate care or provide sufficient notice before withdrawal
Refuse all further follow-up regardless of the clinical need
Transfer the patient elsewhere without any explanation given
w: After accepting a case, continuity of care is owed; withdrawal requires adequate notice so the patient can arrange alternatives. Abandonment or unexplained transfer is unethical.
k: Avoiding patient abandonment is the principle. Choose continuity with proper notice.
decode: After formally undertaking a case, the optometrist should CONTINUE care or give SUFFICIENT NOTICE before withdrawing.
ow: Abandoning the patient without notice is unethical.
Correct. Continue care or give sufficient notice.
Refusing all follow-up despite need is unethical.
Transferring without explanation is unethical.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: In an emergency, an optometrist should:
o: Respond to a request for assistance
w: Professionals should respond to reasonable requests for emergency help within their competence. Refusing outright, demanding payment first or blanket-referring without assessment is improper.
k: Emergency ethics favour responding and helping, not refusing or gating on payment.
decode: In an emergency, an optometrist should RESPOND to a request for assistance (within competence).
ow: Referring every emergency without assessment is improper.
Correct. Respond to the request for assistance.
Refusing assistance automatically is improper.
Demanding payment before assistance is improper.

q: The primary responsibility of an optometrist under RA 8050 is the:
w: The law centres on protecting and promoting the public's visual welfare. Profit, sales and patient volume are business metrics, not the professional's primary duty.
k: Public welfare beats commerce in professional-duty questions. Choose the patient/public option.
decode: The primary responsibility of an optometrist under RA 8050 is the VISUAL WELFARE of the public.
ow: The sale of premium frames is a commercial metric, not the primary duty.
Correct. The visual welfare of the public.
The number of patients seen is a business metric, not the primary duty.
Clinic profitability is a business metric, not the primary duty.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: Professional care should be provided with:
o: Different quality based on social status
w: Equal diligence and non-discrimination are ethical baselines. Varying quality by status, wealth or friendship is unethical.
k: Fairness/equality is the ethical answer; any preferential or discriminatory option is wrong.
decode: Professional care should be provided with EQUAL DILIGENCE to patients.
ow: Different quality by social status is unethical.
Preference for friends is unethical.
Correct. Equal diligence to patients.
Preference for wealthy patients is unethical.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: An optometrist should respect the confidential nature of information concerning:
w: Confidentiality protects patient information. Competitors, suppliers and advertisers are not the subject of the duty of confidentiality.
k: Confidentiality attaches to patients. The non-patient options are distractors.
decode: An optometrist should respect the confidential nature of information concerning PATIENTS served.
ow: Confidentiality is owed to patients, not competitors.
Confidentiality is owed to patients, not suppliers.
Correct. Patients served.
Confidentiality is owed to patients, not advertisers.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: Continuous improvement of theoretical and practical proficiency is:
w: Ongoing competence and lifelong learning are professional responsibilities. It is neither optional, student-only, nor finished at licensure.
k: Continuing competence is a duty, not a choice. Reject the options that make it optional or time-limited.
decode: Continuous improvement of theoretical and practical proficiency is a PROFESSIONAL RESPONSIBILITY.
ow: It is not unnecessary after licensure.
It is not required only for students.
It is not optional.
Correct. A professional responsibility.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: An optometrist should maintain cordial relationships with:
o: Only other optometrists working in the same clinic
Members of the profession and other professions
Only patients who are fully able to pay
Members and suppliers of the optical trade only
w: Professionalism includes collegial relations within optometry and with other health professions. Limiting cordiality to a narrow group is contrary to the code.
k: The inclusive option (own and other professions) beats the exclusive ones.
decode: An optometrist should maintain cordial relationships with members of the PROFESSION and OTHER professions.
ow: It is not limited to same-clinic optometrists.
Correct. Members of the profession and other professions.
It is not limited to paying patients.
It is not limited to the optical trade.

q: The primary objective of an optometric clinic should be:
w: Quality patient care is the clinic's core objective; sound business supports but does not replace it. Maximising sales, advertising or costly lenses puts commerce first.
k: Patient care over profit. The sales/advertising options are commercial traps.
decode: The primary objective of an optometric clinic should be QUALITY PATIENT CARE.
ow: Maximum sales puts commerce first.
Selling the most expensive lenses puts commerce first.
Correct. Quality patient care.
Maximum advertising puts commerce first.

q: A well-organized patient record should contain:
o: Only the total amount that the patient has paid
Only the patient's full name and home address
Only the final spectacle prescription that was given
Relevant clinical findings and management information
w: Good records document history, findings and management for continuity and legal protection. Name, payment or Rx alone is incomplete.
k: "Well-organized record" means comprehensive clinical documentation, not a single field.
decode: A well-organized patient record should contain RELEVANT CLINICAL FINDINGS and management information.
ow: The total amount paid alone is incomplete.
Name and address alone are incomplete.
The final prescription alone is incomplete.
Correct. Relevant clinical findings and management information.

q: Proper record keeping is important because it:
o: Supports continuity and quality of patient care
w: Records enable continuity, quality and accountability. They do not replace examination, guarantee profit or substitute for communicating with the patient.
k: Records support care; they do not replace clinical steps. Pick the continuity/quality option.
decode: Proper record keeping is important because it SUPPORTS CONTINUITY and QUALITY of care.
ow: Correct. It supports continuity and quality.
Records do not replace informed communication.
Records do not guarantee profit.
Records do not eliminate the need for examination.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: Informed consent primarily means that the patient:
o: Receives relevant information and voluntarily agrees
Signs a blank consent form without reading it
Must first purchase glasses before being treated
Is forced to accept the recommended treatment
w: Informed consent is voluntary agreement after receiving adequate information about the procedure, risks and alternatives. Coercion, forced purchase or blank forms are invalid.
k: "Informed" (given information) plus "consent" (voluntary agreement) defines the correct option.
decode: Informed consent primarily means the patient RECEIVES relevant information and VOLUNTARILY AGREES.
ow: Correct. Receives information and voluntarily agrees.
Signing a blank form without reading is not valid consent.
It does not require purchasing glasses first.
Being forced to accept treatment is not consent.

q: Which is an important component of good clinic management?
w: Sanitation and infection control protect patients and staff and are essential management. The other options are examples of poor management.
k: Choose the responsible practice; the other three are obvious negatives.
decode: An important component of good clinic management is PROPER SANITATION and INFECTION CONTROL.
ow: Ignoring expired supplies is poor management.
Poor instrument maintenance is poor management.
Correct. Proper sanitation and infection control.
Unorganized records are poor management.

q: Instruments used in clinical practice should be:
o: Properly maintained and disinfected as appropriate
Used regardless of their actual working condition
Shared between patients without any cleaning
Stored anywhere convenient around the clinic
w: Instruments must be maintained and disinfected to ensure safety and accuracy. Sharing uncleaned, careless storage or using faulty tools risks infection and error.
k: Safety and hygiene wins. The neglectful options are wrong.
decode: Instruments should be PROPERLY MAINTAINED and DISINFECTED as appropriate.
ow: Correct. Properly maintained and disinfected.
Using instruments regardless of condition is unsafe.
Sharing uncleaned instruments risks infection.
Careless storage is improper.

q: A clinic's appointment system is primarily useful for:
w: Appointments organise patient flow and reduce waiting. They have nothing to do with prescription power, diagnosing disease or measuring acuity.
k: An appointment system is an administrative tool, so its purpose is workflow, not clinical measurement.
decode: A clinic's appointment system is primarily useful for MANAGING PATIENT FLOW efficiently.
ow: It does not diagnose glaucoma.
Correct. Managing patient flow efficiently.
It does not measure visual acuity.
It does not increase prescription power.

q: An effective inventory system helps the clinic to:
w: Inventory control tracks stock and avoids shortages or expiry. It does not diagnose, replace exams or measure pressure.
k: Inventory = supplies management. The clinical-sounding options are distractors.
decode: An effective inventory system helps MONITOR supplies and PREVENT shortages.
ow: It does not determine IOP.
Correct. Monitor supplies and prevent shortages.
It does not replace clinical examination.
It does not diagnose refractive errors.

q: Which is an example of unethical business practice?
o: Misleading claims about guaranteed visual results
Accurate disclosure of the professional fees
Proper patient education about their own care
Careful maintenance of accurate clinical records
w: Guaranteeing results with misleading claims deceives patients and is unethical. Accurate disclosure, education and records are ethical practices.
k: Look for the deceptive/misleading option; the honest practices are all acceptable.
decode: An example of unethical business practice is MISLEADING CLAIMS about guaranteed visual results.
ow: Correct. Misleading claims about guaranteed results.
Accurate disclosure of fees is ethical.
Proper patient education is ethical.
Careful maintenance of records is ethical.

q: Professional advertising should be:
o: Truthful and consistent with professional standards
Designed to guarantee a complete cure of disease
False and exaggerated to attract more patients
Based only on misleading promotional claims
w: Advertising must be truthful and standard-compliant. False, exaggerated, cure-guaranteeing or misleading ads violate the code.
k: Only the truthful option is ethical; anything false or guaranteeing cures is wrong.
decode: Professional advertising should be TRUTHFUL and consistent with professional standards.
ow: Correct. Truthful and standard-consistent.
It must not guarantee a complete cure of disease.
It must not be false and exaggerated.
It must not rely on misleading claims.

q: The PRC Professional Regulatory Boards have authority to investigate violations of professional standards and:
w: The boards investigate and adjudicate administrative cases against practitioners. They do not manufacture lenses, run clinics or sell drugs.
k: A regulatory board's power is investigate and adjudicate. The commercial options are out of scope.
decode: The PRC Regulatory Boards investigate violations and ADJUDICATE administrative cases.
ow: They do not operate private clinics.
They do not sell medications.
They do not manufacture lenses.
Correct. Adjudicate administrative cases.

q: The Board of Optometry may, according to law, impose professional regulatory actions including:
o: Closure of every optical shop operating within the region
Cancellation of all prescriptions previously issued nationwide
Imprisonment of the optometrist without any court proceedings
Suspension or revocation of registration for causes provided by law
w: The Board may suspend or revoke registration for causes defined by law. It cannot imprison (a court function), close all shops, or cancel all prescriptions.
k: Administrative bodies act on licenses, not on liberty. Suspension/revocation is the lawful sanction.
decode: The Board may impose SUSPENSION or REVOCATION of registration for causes provided by law.
ow: It cannot close every optical shop in the region.
It cannot cancel all prescriptions nationwide.
It cannot imprison without court proceedings.
Correct. Suspension or revocation of registration.

q: Under the IRR, routine optometric examination should generally be performed in:
o: Premises used appropriately for optometric practice
w: Examinations should occur in premises suitable and authorised for practice, ensuring standards and privacy. Public hallways or unauthorised sites are improper.
k: Proper facility is the safe, standards-based answer; casual public locations are wrong.
decode: Under the IRR, routine examination should be performed in PREMISES used appropriately for optometric practice.
ow: A workplace without authorization is improper.
A shopping mall hallway is improper.
Correct. Appropriate optometric premises.
Any public place is improper.

q: The PRC has specifically issued an advisory concerning unauthorized optometric practice involving:
o: Examination and dispensing through unauthorized mobile units
Reading printed books under normal room lighting
Buying eyeglass frames from an ordinary retail store
Wearing contact lenses purely for cosmetic purposes
w: Advisories target unauthorised mobile examination and dispensing that bypass proper premises and oversight. Wearing lenses, buying frames or reading are not regulated acts.
k: "Unauthorized practice" points to the clinical acts done improperly (mobile units), not harmless consumer activities.
decode: The PRC advisory on unauthorized practice targets EXAMINATION and DISPENSING through unauthorized MOBILE units.
ow: Correct. Unauthorized mobile examination and dispensing.
Reading printed books is not a regulated act.
Buying frames at retail is not a regulated act.
Wearing cosmetic contact lenses is not a regulated act.

q: A mobile optometric service outside the regular clinic may require appropriate permission from:
o: A frame manufacturer that supplies the clinic with its display stock and finished lens blanks
The next-door neighbor of a patient who lives near the proposed community outreach venue
Relevant national/local health authorities and/or the recognized professional organization, as applicable
Any optical salesperson employed at a nearby commercial establishment or shopping mall outlet
w: Off-site services need clearance from the proper health authorities and professional bodies. Neighbours, manufacturers and salespersons have no such authority.
k: Permission comes from official regulators. The unofficial parties are distractors.
decode: A mobile optometric service may require permission from RELEVANT national/local health authorities and/or the professional organization.
ow: A frame manufacturer has no such authority.
A patient's neighbor has no such authority.
Correct. Relevant health authorities and/or the professional organization.
An optical salesperson has no such authority.

q: An optometrist discovers signs suggesting a serious ocular disease outside the scope of routine optometric management. What is the best action?
o: Sell the patient a stronger pair of spectacles instead
Conceal the finding to avoid alarming the patient
Ignore the finding and continue routine care as normal
Refer appropriately and explain the concern to the patient
w: Serious findings beyond scope require timely referral with clear explanation. Concealing, selling glasses or ignoring endangers the patient.
k: Beyond scope plus serious = refer and inform. The care-avoiding and sales options are wrong.
decode: On finding a serious disease beyond routine scope, the best action is to REFER appropriately and EXPLAIN the concern.
ow: Selling stronger spectacles instead endangers the patient.
Concealing the finding is unethical.
Ignoring the finding is unethical.
Correct. Refer appropriately and explain the concern.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: A patient cannot afford the professional fee. Ethical practice emphasizes that:
o: The patient should usually be refused service until able to pay
The patient should generally receive inferior, lower-standard care
The patient's condition should simply be ignored by the clinic
Humanitarian considerations may warrant professional service without charge
w: Ethics allow for humanitarian, sometimes pro bono, service; care quality should not depend on ability to pay. Refusing, ignoring or downgrading care is unethical.
k: Compassion over commerce: the humanitarian option is correct; refusal or lesser care is wrong.
decode: When a patient cannot afford the fee, HUMANITARIAN considerations may warrant service WITHOUT charge.
ow: Refusing service until able to pay is not the ethical emphasis.
Providing inferior care is unethical.
Ignoring the condition is unethical.
Correct. Humanitarian service without charge may be warranted.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: An optometrist tells every patient that a particular lens will "cure all eye diseases." This is:
w: Claiming a lens cures all diseases is false and misleading, breaching professional standards. It is neither appropriate advertising, ethical counseling nor good management.
k: "Cure all" is a classic false-claim signal, so it is misleading conduct.
decode: Telling every patient that a lens will 'cure all eye diseases' is MISLEADING professional conduct.
ow: Correct. Misleading professional conduct.
It is not appropriate advertising.
It is not ethical counseling.
It is not good practice management.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: A patient asks the optometrist to disclose another patient's diagnosis. The optometrist should:
o: Give the information to the patient's friends
w: Another patient's information is confidential and must not be shared. Disclosing, posting or telling friends violates privacy.
k: Third-party medical information is protected, so maintain confidentiality. Every sharing option is wrong.
decode: When asked to disclose ANOTHER patient's diagnosis, the optometrist should MAINTAIN CONFIDENTIALITY.
ow: Correct. Maintain confidentiality.
Giving it to the patient's friends violates privacy.
Posting it online violates privacy.
Disclosing it violates privacy.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: An optometrist is offered a financial incentive by a supplier to recommend a product regardless of patient need. The best response is to:
o: Hide the incentive from the patient entirely
Prioritize patient welfare and professional judgment
Increase the price that is charged to patients
Accept it and recommend the product to everyone
w: Recommendations must serve patient need and professional judgment, not kickbacks. Accepting to push a product, concealing the incentive or raising prices is unethical.
k: Conflict-of-interest questions answer with patient welfare and professional judgment over financial gain.
decode: Offered a financial incentive to recommend a product regardless of need, PRIORITIZE PATIENT WELFARE and professional judgment.
ow: Hiding the incentive is unethical.
Correct. Prioritize patient welfare and professional judgment.
Raising prices to patients is unethical.
Accepting and pushing the product to everyone is unethical.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: An optometrist notices a colleague repeatedly practicing in violation of professional regulations. The ethical response is to:
o: Take appropriate steps consistent with professional and regulatory procedures
Spread the information about the colleague widely on social media platforms
Publicly insult and humiliate the colleague in front of the staff
Ignore the questionable conduct completely and say nothing to anyone
w: Repeated violations should be addressed through proper professional and regulatory channels. Ignoring enables harm; public insult or social media are unprofessional.
k: Use the proper channels: report through regulatory procedures, not by ignoring or shaming.
decode: Seeing a colleague repeatedly violating regulations, TAKE APPROPRIATE STEPS through professional and regulatory channels.
ow: Correct. Use proper professional and regulatory procedures.
Spreading it on social media is unprofessional.
Publicly insulting the colleague is unprofessional.
Ignoring the conduct enables harm.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: A patient requests a prescription without undergoing an appropriate examination. The optometrist should:
o: Ask the optical salesperson to determine it
Explain that appropriate assessment is necessary
w: A prescription must follow proper examination for safety and accuracy. Issuing without exam, delegating to a salesperson or guessing is substandard and unethical.
k: No exam, no valid prescription. The correct answer insists on assessment first.
decode: When a patient requests a prescription without an appropriate exam, EXPLAIN that assessment is necessary first.
ow: Providing it immediately without exam is substandard.
Guessing the prescription is unsafe.
Delegating to a salesperson is improper.
Correct. Explain that appropriate assessment is necessary.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: Which principle best describes ethical optometric practice?
o: Patient welfare, professional competence, honesty, and confidentiality
Advertising and marketing placed before clinical patient care
Profit and personal income placed before patient welfare always
Competition with peers placed before professional cooperation
w: Ethical practice rests on patient welfare, competence, honesty and confidentiality. Profit-first, competition-first and advertising-first options invert the priorities.
k: The comprehensive patient-centred option captures the ethics pillars; the single-value commercial options are wrong.
decode: Ethical optometric practice rests on PATIENT WELFARE, COMPETENCE, HONESTY, and CONFIDENTIALITY.
ow: Correct. Patient welfare, competence, honesty, confidentiality.
Advertising before care inverts the priorities.
Profit before welfare inverts the priorities.
Competition before cooperation inverts the priorities.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: An optometrist should approach new developments in optometry with:
o: Blind acceptance of it without any question
Purely commercial considerations and nothing else
Immediate rejection without any proper review
w: New developments deserve evidence-based, critical appraisal. Blind acceptance, reflex rejection or purely commercial motives are unscientific.
k: Evidence and critical thinking is the professional stance; the extreme and commercial options are traps.
decode: New developments should be approached with SCIENTIFIC JUDGMENT and critical evaluation.
ow: Blind acceptance is unscientific.
Purely commercial motives are unscientific.
Immediate rejection without review is unscientific.
Correct. Scientific judgment and critical evaluation.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: The best overall principle for an optometrist managing a practice is to:
o: Avoid making any referrals to other health professionals at all times
Maximize clinic profit regardless of the patient's real needs
Focus almost exclusively on selling optical retail products
Balance sound management with ethical, competent, patient-centered care
w: Good practice balances viable management with ethical, competent, patient-centred care. Profit-only, product-only or referral-avoiding approaches harm patients.
k: "Best overall principle" wants the balanced, patient-centred option, not a single commercial extreme.
decode: The best overall principle is to BALANCE sound management with ethical, competent, patient-centered care.
ow: Avoiding all referrals harms patients.
Maximizing profit regardless of need harms patients.
Focusing on retail sales harms patients.
Correct. Balance management with patient-centered care.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: The Board of Optometry may investigate violations of:
w: The Board of Optometry is a professional regulatory board, so its jurisdiction is optometry laws and the rules of practice, not traffic, tax, or school matters. Those fall to other agencies entirely.
k: A professional board polices its own profession. The answer must stay inside optometry practice, so reject unrelated legal domains.
decode: The Board of Optometry may investigate violations of OPTOMETRY laws and regulations.
ow: Correct. Optometry laws and regulations.
Traffic laws fall to other agencies.
School regulations fall to other bodies.
Tax laws fall to the BIR.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: According to the Code of Ethics, the optometrist's prime concern should be:
o: Service to humanity and visual welfare
w: The Code puts service to humanity and the patient's visual welfare first. Financial gain, sales volume, and beating competitors are secondary at best and never the prime concern.
k: Ethics questions reward the patient-first option. Any answer about money or competition is the distractor.
decode: The optometrist's prime concern should be SERVICE to HUMANITY and visual welfare.
ow: Correct. Service to humanity and visual welfare.
Sales volume is secondary at best.
Financial gain is secondary at best.
Competition with peers is not the prime concern.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: Financial gain in optometric practice should be:
w: Earning a living is legitimate, but ethics ranks it below professional service to the patient. Making it primary, sole, or above patient welfare all violate the Code.
k: Money is allowed but never first. Choose the option that keeps service ahead of profit.
decode: Financial gain should be SECONDARY to professional service.
ow: Correct. Secondary to professional service.
It should not be the primary consideration.
It must not outrank patient welfare.
It is not the only consideration.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: An optometrist should continuously maintain and improve:
o: Personal business profits above all else
w: Ethics requires an optometrist to keep learning and stay competent, so ongoing improvement of professional knowledge and proficiency is the duty. Advertising, sales, and profit are business concerns, not the core professional obligation.
k: Continuing duty points to competence and knowledge. Anything about selling or profit is the ethical distractor.
decode: An optometrist should continuously maintain and improve PROFESSIONAL KNOWLEDGE and proficiency.
ow: Correct. Professional knowledge and proficiency.
Persuasive advertising skills are a business concern, not the core duty.
Aggressive sales techniques are not the core duty.
Personal profit above all is not the core duty.

sec: H2 Bioethics and Code of Ethics
q: Patient information obtained during professional attendance should generally be:
w: Patient information is confidential and must be protected. Posting it publicly, sharing with competitors, or publishing it online all breach that duty.
k: Confidentiality is the default. Reject any option that exposes patient information to others.
decode: Patient information obtained during professional attendance should be KEPT CONFIDENTIAL.
ow: Posting it publicly breaches confidentiality.
Correct. Kept confidential.
Publishing it online breaches confidentiality.
Sharing it with competitors breaches confidentiality.
